quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Do not use your brakes until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs give information about motorist services. These include rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they help you see the road less.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it is safe.
Passing is not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Why is it important to look far ahead while driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
It allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look ahead on the road to avoid sudden braking or turning. This helps you drive safely, save fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What happens when you slow down just to look at collisions or unusual events?

options.text: It causes traffic congestion.
It prevents rear-end collisions.
It improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or other unusual events. This "rubbernecking" creates traffic congestion.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down on the highway?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park with all four wheels off the main road if you can.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often while driving. This helps you know where nearby vehicles are at all times.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This protects you if a vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you cannot avoid hitting them if the rider makes a sudden stop.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is following you too closely on a multilane highway?

options.text: Speed up to match the speed of the car behind you.
Move into the lane to your right and let the other car pass.
Slow down to frustrate the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the lane to your right and let the other car pass.
questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you in the left lane, move right to let it pass. The left lane is for faster-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What should you turn on at dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow to be seen?

options.text: The instrument panel lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever it is hard to see or be seen. Use low beam headlights whenever you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you put yourself and the rider in danger. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. Falls are most common on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic on a two-lane road.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: You increase your speed before the turn.
Traffic on that street moves to the right.
Traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful when turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. The oil from cars has not yet washed off the pavement, creating a slippery mix with the rain.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Keep looking around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep looking around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss because they hide in blind spots. Always watch carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles pulling trailers may not see you behind them. Increase your distance from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so extra distance helps you see around them.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass if you are sure you can safely change lanes. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes and there is enough space.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking. Pull off the road safely when possible.
